Which column(s) represent enforceable discharge limits for effluent compliance—and whether concentration or load form controls—would change the numeric limit selected for comparison against reported measurements.

This row supplies non-N/A human-health, daily-max, monthly-average, and load values for Aldrin while other limit categories are N/A. Interpreting which of these values is the operative enforceable limit (and whether monthly average vs daily maximum applies) would change exceedance determinations; it also bears on whether Aldrin monitoring/comparison is required versus report-only or not applicable.

Chlordane has distinct numeric values across chronic aquatic, human health, daily-max, monthly-average, and load columns. A different reading of which criterion is binding—or whether aquatic vs human-health protection governs the discharge—would yield different applicable limits and different compliance outcomes, and would affect whether monitoring for Chlordane is in scope.

Toxaphene is one of few rows with acute aquatic, chronic aquatic, human-health, concentration, and load values populated. Interpreting whether acute (0.73) or chronic (0.00854357) aquatic limits apply, or whether effluent limits follow human-health values instead, would materially change the enforceable numeric threshold and any monitoring obligation tied to that parameter.
